title: Quarterly recurring empirical canary (notification-suppression behavioral regression test)
description:
Per ADR-011 release-gate-arbiter STRIDE co-sign supplemental threat #1 (supply-chain Tampering on PnP / Graph SDK): the fitness functions enforce that source TEXT contains 'WelcomeEmailDisabled' or 'sendInvitationMessage:false', but they cannot verify that the underlying Microsoft SDK actually HONORS those flags. A malicious PnP version or future Microsoft regression silently ignores the parameter; mail fires; test passes.

DeltaSetup-j3c covers the initial one-time canary. This bd makes it recurring on a quarterly cadence.

Procedure (per playbook §4.3 step 5):
1. Maintain test user xtsync-canary-1@httbrands with monitored mailbox.
2. Every quarter, run a scripted end-to-end test: create a test M365 Group with WelcomeEmailDisabled, add the canary, query Message Trace, assert zero welcome mail.
3. Same test for B2B invitation: POST /invitations with sendInvitationMessage:false, assert zero mail at canary.
4. Same test for SharePoint /invite: POST with sendInvitation:false, assert zero mail.
5. If ANY canary test fires mail: trigger an incident response (pin all provisioning workflows to dispatch-only, file P0 bd, replay PnP/Graph version diff against last-good canary run).

Cadence: 4×/year, aligned with Microsoft's quarterly release cycle. Implement as a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (cron). Test results retained 7 years as evidence record.

title: Report PnP upstream doc-defect: Add-PnPFileSharingInvite -SendInvitation inverted prose
description:
The PnP PowerShell documentation for Add-PnPFileSharingInvite / Add-PnPFolderSharingInvite contains inverted prose for the -SendInvitation parameter.

The doc reads: 'Specifies if an email or post is generated (false) or if the permission is just created (true)'

This is BACKWARDS relative to:
1. The parameter name itself (-SendInvitation strongly implies present = invite is sent)
2. Example 2 on the same documentation page
3. The underlying Microsoft Graph contract (POST /drives/{id}/items/{id}/invite where sendInvitation:true means email is sent)

Risk to others: anyone reading the doc literally would believe omitting -SendInvitation triggers the email, which would lead them to add the switch defensively — and accidentally send mail.

Action: File a GitHub issue at https://github.com/pnp/powershell/issues with:
- Quote of the offending doc line
- The 3 contradictions above
- Suggested replacement prose (e.g., 'Specifies that a notification email is sent to recipients when present. When omitted, the permission is created silently.')
- Cross-reference to the Graph /invite contract.

Our CI gate does NOT depend on Microsoft fixing this — the fitness function regex catches the switch regardless of the prose. But the upstream fix protects everyone else in the PnP community.

title: Audit and remediate aria-label on non-semantic divs (axe aria-prohibited-attr)
description:
axe-core flags 28 nodes across index.html (19), operations.html (8), msp.html (1) where aria-label is applied to plain <div> elements with no explicit role. Per ARIA in HTML, aria-label is prohibited on generic elements with no role because there is no semantic for the name to apply to. axe marks these incomplete (not violations) because it cannot fully prove implicit name sources, but the underlying rule is real for WCAG 2.2 AAA.

Typical offenders are landmark-ish containers like .hero-systems, .project-route-actions, .decision-grid, .op-command, .op-impact-grid, .msp-status-grid.

For each: choose either (a) add a meaningful role such as role=group, role=region, or role=list with appropriate descendants; (b) replace the <div> with a semantic element (<section aria-labelledby> when a visible heading exists); or (c) drop aria-label if the surrounding context already names the region. Re-run python3 tests/accessibility_axe_audit.py and verify the aria-prohibited-attr incomplete count drops to 0 or is explicitly justified.

Acceptance: axe audit reports 0 aria-prohibited-attr nodes OR remaining nodes have a documented exception in the manual AAA checklist.

title: Quarterly 'your DCE access' digest email (ADR-011 STRIDE EoP compensating control)

- Groups they are a member of
- Teams they are a member of
- Date of grant (from UAL where available)

- Frequency: quarterly initially; may move to monthly after launch as a security hygiene practice

- Templating: source from a SharePoint list of canonical access definitions (one row per (user, site/group/team))
